parts.name: base grip

physics.Basic_description: Cream-colored curved plastic handle forming the lower body of the stapler with a smooth matte finish.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the structural base and hand grip for squeezing the stapler mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the curved handle firmly from the side or bottom to stabilize the object during operation.
physics.reason: Injection molded plastic housing typically has thin walls enclosing air to save weight and material.

parts.description: Cream-colored curved plastic handle forming the lower body of the stapler with a smooth matte finish.
parts.function: Provides the structural base and hand grip for squeezing the stapler mechanism.

parts.name: grip ridge 0

physics.Basic_description: Small green textured pads embedded along the side of the cream handle.
physics.Functional_description: Provides enhanced friction and tactile feedback for the user's fingers to prevent slipping.
physics.Grasped_description: These are contact surfaces for fingers rather than primary grasp points for a robotic gripper.
physics.reason: Small rubber inserts are effectively solid volumes of elastomer.

parts.name: anvil plate

physics.Basic_description: Small rectangular silver metal plate located at the front tip of the base handle.
physics.Functional_description: Serves as the anvil surface against which staple legs are bent and clinched.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flush to be a primary grasp point; avoid grasping here to prevent damage.
physics.reason: Metal anvils must be solid and dense to withstand the impact force of stapling.

parts.description: Small rectangular silver metal plate located at the front tip of the base handle.
parts.function: Serves as the anvil surface against which staple legs are bent and clinched.

parts.name: hinge knuckles

physics.Basic_description: Yellowish blocky plastic components connecting the top arm to the base at the rear pivot.
physics.Functional_description: Forms the bearing surface for the hinge mechanism allowing the top arm to rotate.
physics.Grasped_description: Located at the joint; grasping here would interfere with the mechanism and is not recommended.
physics.reason: Hinge knuckles require structural integrity to transfer load, likely solid or thick-walled plastic.

parts.description: Yellowish blocky plastic components connecting the top arm to the base at the rear pivot.
parts.function: Forms the bearing surface for the hinge mechanism allowing the top arm to rotate.

parts.name: arm shell

physics.Basic_description: Mint green elongated plastic cover forming the upper lever of the stapler with a smooth finish.
physics.Functional_description: Encloses the internal spring and staple magazine while providing the surface for the user to press down.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the top surface or sides of this shell to actuate the stapling mechanism.
physics.reason: This is a cosmetic and protective cover shell, inherently hollow to enclose the internal mechanism.

parts.description: Mint green elongated plastic cover forming the upper lever of the stapler with a smooth finish.
parts.function: Encloses the internal spring and staple magazine while providing the surface for the user to press down.

parts.name: carrier rail

physics.Basic_description: Dark grey metallic strip visible at the rear end of the top arm assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Guides the staple pusher or acts as part of the loading mechanism track.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal/structural component not intended for grasping.
physics.reason: Metal rails in staplers are typically stamped sheet metal or solid bars for rigidity.

parts.description: Dark grey metallic strip visible at the rear end of the top arm assembly.
parts.function: Guides the staple pusher or acts as part of the loading mechanism track.

parts.name: driver blade

physics.Basic_description: Small light blue metallic component protruding slightly from the top arm near the hinge.
physics.Functional_description: Part of the mechanism that pushes the staple out of the magazine.
physics.Grasped_description: Tiny functional part, not suitable for grasping.
physics.reason: Driver blades must be solid metal to transmit force without buckling.

parts.description: Small light blue metallic component protruding slightly from the top arm near the hinge.
parts.function: Part of the mechanism that pushes the staple out of the magazine.

parts.name: hinge pin

physics.Basic_description: Small magenta-colored cylindrical pin located at the center of the hinge connection.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the axle around which the top arm rotates relative to the base.
physics.Grasped_description: Fastener component, too small and critical to grasp.
physics.reason: Pins are solid cylinders designed to resist shear forces.

parts.description: Small magenta-colored cylindrical pin located at the center of the hinge connection.
parts.function: Acts as the axle around which the top arm rotates relative to the base.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
